Over-stated, and the fallback is the right default. probeShallow runs inside the same Promise.all as `git log`; if git were missing or the repo unreadable, the log call throws first and the enclosing catch already returns gitAvailable:false. The only way this handler runs is git older than 2.15, which predates `rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`. Those versions cannot produce a shallow clone this code would need to warn about, so returning false is correct — returning 'unknown' would emit a false historyLimited warning on every scan with old git.
